scenes.title: At the Chapel of the Tide door

beats.speaker: priest
beats.text: The Tide hears any name that's owed it. Bring her to this door, and I'll come out to the step for her. Nobody names the drowned through a shut door.

beats.speaker: sergeant
beats.text: A hooded lamp, set low to look like the Mole. Grayrock will want her hanged for the cargo. The Watch will give her a week for the lighters, and not a day more. Keep the lamp. Your word's enough, and I'll fetch her myself.

triggers.note: Each day: the clerk's and the neighbour's choices, and the lamplighter's while a road is under way.

effect.words: What became of the lighters' crews?
effect.reply: Crews? The Wharf Office reads the losses out on the pier: cargo lost, eh, and a line under it. Same words as for the one that went down in the bay years back. A crew of three, I think, and the ledger calls them cargo. Rough water, to be written down like that.

effect.words: Does your neighbour go out in a blow?
effect.reply: Every blow, with a lamp and a jar, and back at dawn soaked through. She cries on the stair sometimes. Her brother was on a Grayrock lighter, years back. Nobody ever came to say sorry.

effect.words: You lit the lamp on the headland.
effect.reply: And they wrote my brother down as cargo. Cargo lost, a line under it. I light a lamp so the Wharf loses cargo too. Nobody drowns, mostly. I see to that. Mostly.

effect.words: Come and name him at the Tide.
effect.reply: Out loud, at the Chapel of the Tide? All these years and nobody once asked his name. Walk with me, then. I'll put the lamp out on the way.

phases.journal: In fog and in a blow, a lamp burns low on the North Headland rocks where no lamp should be.

effects.text: Mind the North Headland in fog. There's a light there that wants ships.
Full measure to the Lamp Store, and one of their lamplighters buys a jar more of her own on blowy days. Says the wind snuffs her wicks. I've not said a word, and I'd thank you not to say I did.

phases.journal: The false lamp has been traced to an old lamplighter who lost a brother on the wharf. Now it is for the wolves to say what is done with her.

effects.text: The lamplighter's name is out, then. What's done with it is yours to choose. Gently, I said, and I meant it.
You've come about the headland. I know you have. Sit, if you want. I'll not run.

quests.title: A Lamp Where None Should Be
quests.summary: Ships steering for the Mole in fog run onto the North Headland instead. A crane hand on the Wharf wants the false light found.

offer.say: #greet#, #address#. I unload what Grayrock's lighters bring in, and two lighters' worth never came, both onto the North Headland in fog, steering for a light low on the rocks as if it were the Mole. Take the true bearing at the Bay Light, walk North Cove, then find me that other light after dark.
offer.accept: The Bay Light, then the rocks after dark.
offer.handIn: Here's the lamp from the rocks.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. A lamp in a hood, set low to look like the Mole. City oil, the Lamp Store's own; I'd know the stink anywhere. One of the lamplighters, then. I know a story about that House and the wharf I won't repeat. Follow the oil, gently.
